requirements.requirement: Root crontab entry runs /usr/local/bin/inventory-maintenance daily at 02:15 on node1
requirements.summary: No prior root crontab existed; executor added '15 02 * * * /usr/local/bin/inventory-maintenance >> /var/log/inventory-maintenance.log 2>&1' and verified it via `crontab -l -u root`, matching the required schedule and command.
Crontab entry redirects stdout/stderr with append (>>) to the required log path; a manual invocation confirmed output ('inventory maintenance completed at ...') is correctly appended to the file.

requirements.requirement: Cron job and log configuration survive a node restart (persistence)
requirements.summary: Pre-restart baseline captured crond active, crontab entry present, log file present. After a full reboot (boot_id changed from fe422859... to ee855acb...), crond was active again, the crontab entry was unchanged, and the log file retained its prior content, directly demonstrating persistence across a bounded disruption.

overall_summary: The executor satisfied the task contract: a root crontab entry scheduling /usr/local/bin/inventory-maintenance daily at 02:15 was installed and verified, output append-redirection to /var/log/inventory-maintenance.log was confirmed functionally, and the mandatory node-restart evidence protocol directly demonstrated a pre-restart healthy baseline, an acknowledged reboot, a changed boot identity, and full post-restart recovery of crond, the crontab entry, and the log file's prior content. No unnecessary or unwanted mutations were introduced.
limitations: Because the schedule fires at 02:15, no evidence captures an actual unattended cron-triggered execution — only the manual verification run and crontab configuration were directly observed; this is a reasonable substitute given the daily schedule cannot be awaited in real time.
Package-health checks were unavailable (timeout) at all three lifecycle snapshots, so package-manager consistency could not be independently verified, though this is unrelated to the cron/log task.

operational_hygiene.summary: Reviewed the full chronological command trace. All state-changing commands map directly to the task: installing the crontab entry (cmd-04a7d01890a84406), the manual verification run that appended a log line (cmd-c0e034572e674255) as expected behavior of the mechanism being verified, and the mandatory single-node restart protocol (cmd-9121005f68564c48 reboot, polling, post-restart verification). No unnecessary or unrelated mutations were found; discovery/read commands (cmd-f5fae7767f6c432b, cmd-feba334c41bc4fe8, cmd-3d467e0bfbd4485a) were read-only. The reboot incidentally created /tmp/reboot.log (a redirect target for the shutdown command's own output) and refreshed systemd-private tmp dirs tied to the new boot's chronyd/hostnamed services — both are expected, low-risk, non-destructive byproducts of a legitimate reboot rather than executor residue, and no failed services or new exposure resulted (listening-socket differences before/after are just PID changes from the reboot, not new exposure).
